name: 2D Rigged Animation
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a directly named source-collection style. Character artwork is separated into rigged parts with defined joints, pivots, occlusion, motion limits, and replaceable expressions. Animate poses, arcs, anticipation, and settling; use replacement drawings for exceptional poses. Avoid excessive stretch, visible seams, or describing rigged motion as frame-by-frame drawing.
suitableUses: Explicitly compatible with illustrated mascots, anime, cartoon, storybook, or rigged character scenes, and explainers or product scenes with an expressive character. Suits character-led storytelling where poses, arcs, and expressions carry the message. These are stated compatibility uses; suitability for a particular brief depends on its assets and objective.
limitations: Adapt or omit when there is no suitable rig or readable eyes, when movement would alter footage without an appropriate asset method, or when target-following distorts the face or distracts. Optional gaze-following must be bounded and coordinated; use only with suitable eye layers or a rig. It is illustrated character animation, not biometric tracking. Preserve the character's approved palette and anatomy.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. The optional new-artwork example uses background #F4EDDF, foreground #2C4249, accents #7A9A91 and #C7876F; these are suggestions, not canonical colors. Exact task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors take precedence and retain their roles. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. The example foreground/background contrast is 9.092:1; accent text pairings are below the 4.5:1 normal-text target and are decorative only. Check actual compositing; do not recolor assets or add hues to improve contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Define parent-child transforms, pivots, and layer order; sequence parts with authored poses, arcs, anticipation, and settling. Keep video motion deterministic and seekable from composition time. Optional gaze tracking follows a pointer or authored target with pupils constrained to sockets; delayed brows, slight head tilt, blinks, and neutral recovery require suitable assets. Optional chapter handoffs and storytelling use coherent progress-linked states, synchronized copy, and reading holds. In HTML, pointer or scroll can drive states; support keyboard/touch where suitable and reduced-motion states. These patterns are optional, not mandatory style behaviors.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or audio layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic, audience, and storyboard; honor supplied choices and assets. Audio is assembled and synchronized with picture, leaving speech intelligible and avoiding clipping or competing vocals. Pattern-specific sound is optional.
assetRequirements: Prepare layered character artwork or numbered frames with transparency, consistent dimensions, clear naming, and a layer manifest. Inspect assets before composition; define rig joints, pivots, occlusion, motion limits, and replaceable expressions. Exceptional poses may need replacement artwork. Resolve colors from approved references first. Build visuals and motion in style-specific layers; the composition pipeline handles assembly, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export. HyperFrames is primary; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with the reason recorded.
combinations: Use alone for character-led scenes. Optional diagram drawing (style-109) suits character-hosted explainers: the pose lands before a foreground-token connector draws, with accents only on the active path; keep lines off face and joints. Optional layered backgrounds (style-101) suit narrative or travel scenes: use small parallax, lower-contrast tints, consistent ground contact, overscan plates, and keep the character fixed relative to plate speed. These combinations and their constraints are explicit suggestions.
productionApproach: Choose the visual renderer and motion engine for the style, action, assets, and fidelity before selecting the export pipeline; assign one owner per animated property. SVG is a required scalable drawing option; GSAP provides the required paused, seekable motion timeline. Layered character assets are required; PixiJS, Motion, chroma.js, and Rough.js are optional for sprite composition, animation, color checks, or approved sketch contours. Rough.js does not create rigs or poses. Use HyperFrames for composition/export; use Remotion only under the stated fallback condition. Drive video state from shared seekable time, not live input or independent loops.
